headline: South Korea's stock market, a star of the AI trade earlier this year, is losing investors as trading dries up and foreign money leaves.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: a fresh Bloomberg analysis with exchange figures, read in full and not overstated, since the Kospi is still among 2026's best performers.
importance_line: What changed is that a market that led the AI trade now has collapsing turnover and heavy foreign selling, which matters first to savers and pension holders with Korean or Asian shares in their funds, then to foreign funds and local retail investors, then to Samsung and SK Hynix, and the doubt is that Bloomberg notes the Kospi is still among 2026's best performers and some investors see buying chances.
summary: Bloomberg reports that trading in South Korea's $4.3 trillion stock market has fallen 70% from its late-May peak, foreign funds have withdrawn $131 billion this year, the most in Asia, and the Kospi, the main index, has lost 22% since the first half ended, when it led major markets. Bloomberg links the slump to the index's reliance on two memory-chip makers, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which make up over half of its weight, as investors doubt how long the memory-chip boom will last and some shift to Taiwan.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403); full Bloomberg text read on Business Standard, which carries it with the Bloomberg byline, so Bloomberg is the source and the link is Bloomberg's original. Our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried the earlier Bloomberg report that Taiwan had overtaken Korea.
